text:
Sam L: Heads up — after the kernel-selection tweak last night I started seeing rare memory spikes on a few canaries when we feed very long contexts (>64k tokens). Not sure if it's allocator or KV pages.
Anya R: @Sam L can you paste the host/log id? we had one similar but thought it was a batching regression.
Sam L: host: infer-rt-canary-12, logs: /var/log/redwood/runtime/2026-03-17.log excerpt below: 
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:03Z] kvpage: write_complete shard=23 page=412 len=8192 flags=partial
[2026-03-17T02:14:03Z] kvpage: eviction started shard=23 page=412
[2026-03-17T02:14:03Z] mem: alloc growth +6MB
[2026-03-17T02:14:04Z] request: id=abcd-1234 tokens=70000 ctx_len=70000
[2026-03-17T02:14:04Z] kvpage: read shard=23 page=412 return=OK checksum=0x0
[2026-03-17T02:14:04Z] kvcache: stale-token-detected request=abcd-1234
```
Notable: write_complete flagged partial. read returned checksum 0x0 which is suspicious.
Mike D: checksum 0x0 often means 'not set' — could be we skip checksum on hot writes for perf and a race leaves garbage. Do we have replication/commit ordering for page writes?
Anya R: Our code path: write->mark-valid->install-index. We skipped atomic fsync for small pages in the last perf patch. Maybe the mark-valid can race with eviction.
Elaine C: kv-monitor-bot just fired a contamination alert earlier today for that shard on two hosts (same canary group). @kv-monitor-bot any additional metadata?
kv-monitor-bot: alert_id=KVCONT-20260317-001; hosts=[infer-rt-canary-12,infer-rt-canary-15]; common_shard=23; top_signals=[partial_write, stale_read, mem_growth];
Sam L: Repro attempt: I ran a replay script to send two interleaved requests that overwrite the same page during heavy KV eviction. I can reproduce ~1/200 runs. Script attached (short psuedo): 
```
# stress_kvpage_repro.py (pseudo)
for i in range(2000):
  start_request(tokens=70000)
  sleep(0.003)
  priming_write(shard=23,page=412,data=random_chunk())
  wait_done()
```
When it fails, subsequent reads from that page expose tokens from previous requests (cross-request contamination).
Mike D: That sounds like a partial-commit window where eviction swaps page metadata but the content buffer points to reused memory. Two hypotheses: 1) mark-valid flips before copy completes; 2) page recycling pool returns buffers without zeroing.
Anya R: I instrumented the runtime to add tracepoints around page alloc/copy/commit. Short trace: 
```
TRACE: alloc_buf id=0x7f9a3c len=8192
TRACE: copy_from_user -> buf=0x7f9a3c wrote=8192
TRACE: commit_page meta.marked_valid=1 -> install_index(shard=23,page=412)
TRACE: free_pool return id=0x7f9a3c (no-zero)
TRACE: alloc_buf id=0x7f9a3c reused for new write
TRACE: read_page -> returned buf=0x7f9a3c with old tokens
```
Anya R: So allocator is returning same buffer before background zeroing or before copy completes on some slow hosts. The mark_valid path doesn't wait for memory zero or for full write to complete.
Sam L: I also saw that kernel selection change increased concurrency on the page pool because we now batch more kernels per GPU and more sw threads race on the allocator. Makes sense it surfaced now.
Elaine C: Immediate mitigation: can we change page install order to copy->flush->mark_valid so readers only see valid pages? That adds a tiny latency but fixes correctness. We can gate it behind a runtime flag for canaries.
Mike D: Also consider adding inline checksum when mark_valid flips — readers validate checksum and if mismatch, they fallback to safe path (recompute or skip cache). Cheaper than full zeroing.
Anya R: I'll open a PR with two changes: 1) ensure commit sequence enforces memory write completion (memory barrier + write ordering) before mark_valid. 2) when freeing buffers put them on a quarantined list for N ms or zero them before reuse. Add runtime flag `kv.strict_commit=true`.
Sam L: Repro script shows failure rate drops to ~0 with strict_commit on canaries. I'll schedule a 30-min canary rollout for `infer-rt-canary-*`.
kv-monitor-bot: scheduled canary rollout job id=CR-20260317-07 window=30m targets=infer-rt-canary-12,infer-rt-canary-15
Elaine C: Also add a short-lived regression alert for cross-request contamination (sensitivity high) so we catch any residue in prod.
Mike D: For longer term: evaluate allocator change to always zero on return or use pools tagged by lifetime to avoid reuse of hot buffers. Also we should add a per-page CRC stored atomically with metadata. Saves us from subtle races.
Anya R: Opening RFC doc referencing this thread and perf tradeoffs. Draft link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/kvpage-commit-atomicity (WIP)
Sam L: Thanks everyone. Action items: Anya PR + tests, Mike evaluate checksum perf overhead, Elaine add alert and schedule canary, I'll run repro and collect heap/trace dumps. Follow-up in ~2 hours. :thumbsup:
